items.title: Eric Brown Interview, 1969-10-26
items.q: The interviewee, Eric Brown, is introduced by the interviewer as a guest commentator. The name 'Ron Warren' appears only in the interviewer's self-introduction ('This is Ron Warren, your host') and in the context of the show's production. There is no evidence in the transcript of a personal or profe

ctx.x: This is Ron Warren inviting you to come with me as we enter those swinging doors to Speakeasy Junction where they play that good old Dixieland jazz. We'll be here enjoying some of the finest in Dixieland and traditional jazz from every era of jazz history with special emphasis on the music of the 1920s, the golden era of the music we enjoy. So sit back and relax with your bathtub booze while we listen to some of the finest music ever to be called jazz.

Charleston, Charleston, made in Carolina. Some dance, some dance. I'll say there's nothing finer than the Charleston, Charleston. Boy, how you can shuffle. Every step you do, this is something new. Man, I'm telling you, it's a lot of zoopock dance. Wing dance will be a back number. But the Charleston, the new Charleston, that dance is surely a come. But sometimes you'll dance it one time. The dance called the Charleston, when it's off your line.
